summary: Drought monitoring and environmental assessment often involve complex satellite datasets that are difficult for communities and decision-makers to interpret. HULAW addresses this by integrating NASA Earth observation data (POWER, GPM IMERG, SMAP, and MODIS) into an interactive environmental monitoring platform. Featuring a 3D globe and an AI agent, it transforms satellite observations into accessible visualizations and contextual insights, helping farmers, local governments, and disaster response teams better understand environmental conditions and make informed decisions for drought preparedness.
details:
HULAW is an Earth observation and environmental monitoring platform designed to make satellite-derived environmental information more accessible, understandable, and useful for decision-making. By utilizing NASA Earth observation data, geospatial visualization, and an integrated AI agent, HULAW helps users explore environmental conditions, monitor drought-related indicators, and better understand changes occurring across different geographical areas.

At its core, HULAW utilizes multiple NASA Earth observation resources to examine different aspects of drought. NASA POWER provides precipitation data for analyzing rainfall patterns, while NASA's Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) mission, particularly IMERG, provides satellite-based precipitation observations. Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) data supports the assessment of soil moisture conditions, while Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) data provides vegetation-related observations to help evaluate vegetation health and greenness. By bringing these complementary environmental indicators together, HULAW provides a more comprehensive perspective on drought conditions rather than relying on rainfall measurements alone.

The platform processes environmental datasets through a Python and FastAPI backend, transforming satellite observations into meaningful indicators, historical comparisons, and visual representations. Its interactive frontend, developed using React and TypeScript with CesiumJS, allows users to explore geographical areas through an interactive globe, visualize environmental conditions, examine historical trends, and understand how indicators change over time.

A key component of HULAW is its integrated AI agent, which acts as an intelligent interface between users and environmental information. It allows users to interact with the platform through natural language, explore drought-related information, and receive contextual explanations about environmental indicators and observed conditions. Rather than requiring users to interpret complex satellite datasets independently, the AI agent helps bridge the gap between technical Earth observation information and practical human understanding.

HULAW is intended to support farmers, local government units, disaster risk reduction offices, researchers, and other stakeholders who need accessible environmental information. By combining NASA's publicly available Earth observation resources with geospatial analysis and AI-assisted interpretation, the platform aims to support evidence-informed agricultural planning, environmental awareness, and proactive drought preparedness.

What makes HULAW distinctive is its integration of multiple NASA Earth observation resources, geospatial analytics, and an interactive AI agent within a unified platform. It demonstrates how publicly available space-based data can be transformed into accessible environmental insights, helping communities better understand changing environmental conditions and respond to climate-related challenges.
